chunks: Al-Hasan ibn al-Zibriqan al-Tabari narrated to me through his own chain, elevating it to al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said:

I said, 'Sometimes when we visit the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), it is difficult for us to perform Ghusl for the visitation due to the cold or other reasons.' He (peace be upon him) replied, 'Whoever performs Ghusl in the Euphrates and visits al-Husayn (peace be upon him), an incalculable amount of merit is recorded for him. And whenever he returns to the place where he performed Ghusl and performs Wuďū and visits al-Husayn (peace be upon him), that same reward is recorded for him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing Wuďū instead of Ghusl before Ziyarah if one previously bathed in the Euphrates?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a specific legal concession (rukhsah) for pilgrims who find the cold of the Euphrates River prohibitive for full ritual bath (Ghusl), allowing them to perform only ablution (Wudu) at the same location. This hadith highlights the unique spiritual status of the Euphrates (Al-Furat) as a sacred site where the physical act of purification is intrinsically linked to the merit of the visit, ensuring that the reward for Ziyarah is not diminished by practical hardships. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing ritual purity with accessibility, affirming that the sanctity of the place amplifies the reward even when the full ritual is abbreviated.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 6. Ḥasan ibn Zibriqān Al-Ťabari narrated to me through his Isnād, from someone who said:

I said to Imam Sādiq (a.s.), “Sometimes when we go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.), it is difficult to perform Ghusl because of the cold (climate) or for other reasons.” Imam (a.s.) replied, “So many merits will be registered for those who go to the Euphrates (River) and perform Ghusl in it before going to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.), that they cannot be counted. And if they return anytime (in the future) to the place where they performed Ghusl, and (instead) perform Wuďū before going to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.), the same (extent of) rewards will be registered for them.”
